header.prereleaseNotice: Pre-release v{{version}} is available. It is shown here only and does not count as a required update.
header.title: Admin Dashboard
header.subtitle: Manage invite codes, users, roles, badges and security.
header.criticalRequired: A critical or security update is required.
header.criticalBody: Deleting users and changing roles, badges, tiers or invite bans is disabled until the app is updated. Other administration continues to work.

queue.searchPlaceholder: Search claimant name, email or work URL…

detail.dismissed: Report dismissed. The claimant has been emailed the outcome.
detail.counterRecorded: Counter-notice recorded. Hash bans lifted; accounts stay disabled until reviewed.
detail.deleteConfirm:
Deleting this report permanently removes it — the claimant's record is gone.

Its hashes are un-banned first, so a hash ban is NOT kept after deleting the report.

Continue?
detail.takeDownBody: Pick the reported files. Every account's copy of the same bytes is removed, the hashes are banned, and the owners' accounts are disabled.
detail.dismissBody: Records the decision as no action needed. The claimant is emailed the outcome.
detail.dismissPlaceholder: Why is no action being taken?
detail.counterBody: The reported party disputes the claim. Their hash bans are lifted, but their accounts stay disabled until you re-activate them on the Disabled accounts view.
detail.deleteBody: Removes the report row entirely. Its hashes are un-banned first, so this is not a way to keep a ban alive. Use it only for junk or mistaken filings.

media.empty: No media files match. Try a username or check the hash.
media.notePlaceholder: Optional note recorded with the decision.
media.result: Removed {{files}} file{{s}}, banned {{hashes}} hash{{es}} and disabled {{accounts}} account{{s}}.
media.takeDownSubtitle: Every account holding the same bytes is affected. Accounts are disabled only when you tick the box below.
media.disableOwnerPrompt: Reason for disabling @{{username}}. It is recorded on the account and the user can appeal.
media.takeDownProfileRowConfirm:
Take down EVERY media file owned by @{{username}} (profile /u/{{slug}})?

All their uploads are removed and their hashes banned. Their account stays enabled.

This cannot be undone. Continue?

manual.banHashBody: Blocks the bytes anywhere, with no report. A future upload with the same SHA-256 (or perceptual twin) is rejected.
manual.profileBody: Removes every media file owned by the profile's owner and bans their hashes. Enter a profile slug or id.
manual.profileNotePlaceholder: Optional note recorded with the bans.
manual.profileRefRequired: A profile slug or id is required.
manual.profileFailed: Could not take down the profile
manual.disableBody: Locks the account out (sign-in blocked) with a recorded reason. The user can appeal; it never deletes data.
manual.accountRefRequired: A username or user id is required.
manual.accountConfirm:
Disable the account "{{ref}}"?

They can appeal. Continue?

hashes.unbanConfirm: Lift this hash ban? Un-banning means the same bytes can be uploaded again by any account.
hashes.footer: Un-banning restores the original files by bytes, not as stored copies. Use it for false positives — lifting does not touch any account state.

disabled.reactivatePrompt: Decision note for re-activating @{{username}}. This is recorded on the account and is never shown to the user.
disabled.footer: Re-activation is always a manual operator decision. A counter-notice lifts the hash bans but never turns an account back on by itself.

inviteSettings.userGenerationDescription: Allow non-admin users to generate invite codes. Role quotas and event allowances still apply; invite-banned users stay excluded.
inviteSettings.disabled: Disabled — users with a generation-enabled role still need this switch on.

inviteEvent.title: Invite event
inviteEvent.description: Grant every non-banned user an invite allowance. They generate the codes themselves; the allowance and any code created from it expire on the chosen date.
inviteEvent.granted: Granted {{count}} user(s) {{each}} invite credit(s) each, expiring {{date}}.

roles.adminNote: The Admin role always has every permission. The User role and custom roles can be edited here.
roles.name: Name
roles.inviteGenerationDescription: Requires the "Generate own invite codes" permission. Batch limit 0 disables role-based generation. Outstanding limit 0 = unlimited. Cooldown 0 = none. Expiry bounds apply to every code the role generates.
roles.heading: Roles
roles.locked: Locked until the app is updated

badges.description: Badges appear on profiles as colored icons. Pick a label, color and lucide icon name.
badges.label: Label
badges.internalIdHint: Machine-readable identifier. Auto-generated from the label when empty.
badges.heading: Badges
badges.locked: Locked until the app is updated

allowlist.title: IP Allowlist
allowlist.description: IPs or CIDR networks that bypass the anti-abuse fingerprint guard: users on them can register multiple accounts (e.g. beta testers) and are exempt from login lockouts even if the network was flagged. Stored in the database, so it survives redeploys.

bans.title: Auth Bans & Lockouts
bans.description: Automatically applied to fingerprints (IP, cookie, user agent) and accounts after repeated failed auth attempts. Remove a record to allow access again.

authLog.title: Auth Log
authLog.description: Failed auth attempts with the applied penalty. Entries are pruned automatically once their lock expires or after the retention period.

domains.title: Custom Domains
domains.description: Self-serve custom domain requests. Users prove ownership with a TXT record; review verified requests and activate or reject them here.
domains.removeTitle: Remove this custom domain and its TLS certificates

invitePurchase.title: Paid invite credits
invitePurchase.description: Let people buy invite credits. Purchased credits land on the buyer's balance and never expire; a guest who buys before registering gets codes by email instead.
invitePurchase.noPacksPriced: No packs are priced, so nothing can be sold yet. Set INVITE_PRICE_PACKS (for example 1:100,3:200,10:600) and restart the backend. An empty pack list keeps the store closed whatever this switch says.
invitePurchase.mailNotConfiguredTitle: Mail is not configured — guest buyers cannot be delivered
invitePurchase.mailNotConfiguredBody: The store is on, so you are taking money right now, but this instance has no working outbound mail. A guest who buys before registering receives their invite codes by email only, and that email cannot be sent: confirm one of their orders and they will have paid for something they cannot reach.
invitePurchase.mailConfigHint: Configure a real mailbox before you take another order — a Gmail address with an app password is the quickest route. Set SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, SMTP_FROM_EMAIL and SMTP_ENABLED=true, then recreate the backend.
invitePurchase.mailConfigFulfil: Until then you can still fulfil by hand: use Copy claim link on any paid guest order below and send the buyer that link over whatever channel you already have with them. That link is the only thing you need — it does not reveal the codes themselves.
invitePurchase.resaleDescription: Whether the Terms let a member sell an invite code onwards. This is a published legal position, so it is not tied to the store switch above.

resaleModes.offHelp: The Terms say nothing about selling invite codes onwards.
resaleModes.permittedHelp: Publishes an explicit resale permission, so a member selling their codes is acting on the Terms. Nothing is blocked or tracked.
resaleModes.legalHelp: An explicit resale prohibition is published. Codes are not tracked by origin.
resaleModes.enforcedHelp: Publishes the prohibition and records where purchased codes came from, so the platform can answer that question.

invitePurchase.noPurchases: No invite credits have been bought yet.
invitePurchase.copyClaimLinkTitle: Re-issues this buyer's claim link so you can deliver it yourself. Does not reveal the codes.
invitePurchase.markRefundedTitle: Records the refund and revokes unspent credits. Does not refund at the payment provider.
invitePurchase.refundConfirm:
Return the money at {{provider}} first.

This only records the refund here and revokes the unspent credits and codes from this purchase. Anything already redeemed stays valid.

Continue?
invitePurchase.refundFooter: Refunding revokes the unspent codes and credits from that purchase. Codes someone has already redeemed stay valid — that person has joined.
invitePurchase.loadFailed: Could not load invite purchase settings.
invitePurchase.recordedRefunded: Recorded as refunded. Unspent credits and codes from that purchase were revoked — remember to return the money at the payment provider.
invitePurchase.claimLinkFailed: Could not create a claim link.
invitePurchase.claimLinkCopiedEmailed: Claim link copied. They were already emailed one — this is a fresh link for the same codes, valid {{days}} days.
invitePurchase.claimLinkCopied: Claim link copied. Send it to the buyer yourself — they were never emailed one.

policy.title: Legal policies
policy.noticePending: Version {{version}} is live and has not been announced yet. Accounts that have not accepted are blocked from signing in until they do.
policy.autoAcceptEnabled: Accounts holding {{roles}} are recorded as accepting each new policy version automatically — but only once the 30-day review window has passed{{window}}
policy.autoAcceptWindowOpen: , which it has for this version.
policy.autoAcceptEnabledSuffix: Until then those accounts must click through like anyone else, or they stay blocked out of this panel.
policy.autoAcceptDisabled: Disabled on this instance. Staff accounts click through the acceptance screen like any other account and can be locked out until they do.
policy.autoAcceptConfigHint: Change it with POLICY_ADMIN_AUTO_ACCEPT and POLICY_ADMIN_AUTO_ACCEPT_ROLES, then recreate the backend. Automatic acceptances are recorded with a marker, so the audit trail never claims a person consented when the platform recorded it.
policy.noteLabel: Note included in the notice email
policy.noteHint: Optional. Shown above the document links so users know why they are being asked again.
policy.notePlaceholder: e.g. We clarified how long we keep analytics data.
policy.emailChangeNoticeHint: Sends to accounts that have not accepted yet, 500 per run. Repeat runs pick up where the last one stopped.
policy.mailNotConfigured: Mail is not configured on this instance, so no email can be sent. The consent gate still applies — users are asked to accept when they sign in.
policy.unreachableNone: No account had a verified mailbox to send to.

seasonalThemes.title: Seasonal Themes
seasonalThemes.description: Schedule seasonal and holiday themes that are applied to user profiles. A globally active theme overrides the user's custom appearance while it's live.
seasonalThemes.toggleSeasonalThemesHint: Master switch for all seasonal features
seasonalThemes.toggleAutoScheduleHint: Apply themes automatically within their date windows
seasonalThemes.toggleRespectPreferenceHint: Let users disable seasonal decorations in Appearance
seasonalThemes.heading: Themes
seasonalThemes.alwaysOnTitle: Always allowed for users who opt in (e.g. Christmas)
seasonalThemes.label: Label

toasts.enterIpOrCidr: Enter an IP address or CIDR network.
toasts.banConfirm:
Ban "{{username}}" from invites?

They can no longer generate invite codes or receive invite-event allowances. Their unused invites are revoked immediately and their remaining allowance is zeroed.
toasts.deleteUserConfirm:
Permanently delete user "{{username}}"?

This erases their account, all profiles, badges, webhooks, passkeys, invite codes, auth logs and uploads from the database and disk. This is irreversible (GDPR erasure).
toasts.deleteRoleConfirm: Delete this role? Users with this role must be reassigned first.
toasts.deleteBadgeConfirm: Delete this badge? It will be removed from all profiles and users.
toasts.removeDomainConfirm:
Remove custom domain "{{domain}}"?

This permanently deletes the request, removes any TLS certificates for it from disk, and regenerates the nginx custom-domain configuration. You will also need to delete its DNS records. Continue?
